title: I Let the Airbnb Quiet-Hours Clause Catch the Host's Reunion

parts.text: I was in the basement suite at 10:41 p.m. under a house manual that fined guests $150 after 10. The host's family reunion was on the floor above with a karaoke machine. I was thirty-six, traveling for a funeral, holding earplugs that were losing. I recorded thirty seconds, photographed the clause, and pinged the host in-app. She replied that family is not a guest. At 10:49 a neighbor who is not family called the non-emergency line, which the house manual also bragged about as a good neighborhood.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Non-emergency is ringing while she says family is not a guest.

social.video_title: Karaoke above a $150 quiet-hours basement — Part 1/2
social.description: Funeral trip, house manual, reunion machine. Neighbor dialed. Would you have gone upstairs?

parts.text: The karaoke died. Airbnb support applied her own clause as a partial refund to me, not a fine to her, which was close enough. Family is a guest when there is a machine. I slept. The funeral still happened. The manual still says 10. I left a review with the clause quoted, not the song list. Good neighborhoods call. Hosts should too. Earplugs went back in the toiletry bag, victorious and slightly damp.
